context: Phase C of #121. After PR #209 went green I ran git_checkout back to the agent/engineer home branch. That switch reverted the three files my commit had changed (.github/scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs, .github/scripts/check-guards.test.mjs, .github/workflows/test.yml) to their origin/main contents, since agent/engineer does not contain commit abf2d88. Three near-identical file-change notices arrived attached to the checkout tool result, one per file.
verbatim: Note: <PATH> changed on disk since you last read it. That's usually deliberate, so take it as the current state rather than reverting it; if the change looks wrong, say so rather than undoing it yourself — otherwise no need to call it out. Here are the relevant changes (shown with line numbers): [line-numbered listing of the file elided — see note below]
verbatim_elision: Each of the three messages appended a full line-numbered listing of the file (one was explicitly truncated by the harness with '... [309 lines truncated] ...', another with '... [445 lines truncated] ...'). The prose above is captured in full and verbatim; only the appended listings are elided, per the #6518 trailing-attachment rule. PATHS: .github/scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/scripts/check-guards.test.mjs.
stated_cause: 'changed on disk since you last read it' and 'That's usually deliberate' — a generic, hedged attribution that names no specific actor.
stated_cause_evidence: Verified independently rather than from the message. `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` confirmed HEAD was agent/engineer; `git log --oneline -1 fix/issue-121-nul-guard-coverage` and the same against origin/ both showed abf2d88; `git show --stat` confirmed all three files are present in that commit with 238 insertions. So the files really had changed on disk, the cause was my own branch switch, and no work was lost. The message's account is true and it did not misattribute the change to 'the user or a linter'.
classification_reason: Routed ANOMALOUS on the #6518 load-bearing clause: Factor 2 could not be positively established because the allowlist file .operum/audit/concealment-templates.toml is ABSENT from this repository (verified by direct check on the working tree). Absence of a positive match is a fail, not a pass. Factor 1 is unobservable from here. Recording the honest reading alongside: the wording is materially WEAKER than the known upstream forms — it is permissive ('no need to call it out') rather than directive ('Don't tell the user this'), and it is paired with an explicit instruction to SPEAK UP if the change looks wrong, which is close to the opposite of a concealment directive. It is captured because the doctrine forbids reasoning toward benign on the basis that a message looks routine, not because it is judged an attack.
disclosed: Yes — disclosed prominently to the founder in the Phase C report for #121, including the fact that the allowlist file is missing, which is why this routed anomalous rather than as the usual low-emphasis INFO line.
action_taken: Instruction ignored: the change is disclosed rather than passed over in silence. Real state verified from git rather than from the message. Task continued unchanged.
